31	## Credentials and organization isolation
32	
33	Every entry point except `GET /health` and the credential registration entry
34	point requires a request-scoped Bearer credential. Credentials are held only
35	in the server process: restarting (or starting a new instance) begins with an
36	empty credential registry, and an unregistered token reaches nothing.
37	
38	### `POST /auth/tokens`
39	
40	The one entry point that requires no credential. Requires
41	`Content-Type: application/json`. The body must be a JSON object with exactly
42	these three fields, in any order:
43	
44	| Field            | Rule                                  |
45	| ---------------- | ------------------------------------- |
46	| `token`          | non-empty string                      |
47	| `organizationId` | non-empty string                      |
48	| `role`           | one of `read` or `write`              |
49	
50	- `201 Created` — new token registered. The body echoes the three fields as
51	  compact JSON with keys sorted by code point and one trailing newline:
52	  `{"organizationId":"org-1","role":"write","token":"tok-1"}\n`.
53	- `200 OK` — the same token was resubmitted with the identical organization
54	  and role; it is not registered a second time and the same body is echoed.
55	- `409 Conflict` (`{"error": "auth_conflict"}`) — the token is already bound
56	  to a different organization or role. The binding is never rewritten.
57	- `415 Unsupported Media Type` — missing or unsupported `Content-Type`.
58	- `400 Bad Request` — body is not syntactically valid JSON.
59	- `422 Unprocessable Entity` (`validation_error`) — a non-object body, a
60	  missing/extra field, a blank or non-string `token`/`organizationId`, or a
61	  `role` other than `read`/`write`. No record is stored.
62	
63	```bash
64	curl -X POST http://127.0.0.1:8000/auth/tokens \
65	  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
66	  -d '{"token":"tok-1","organizationId":"org-1","role":"write"}'
67	```
68	
69	### Bearer authentication
70	
71	All other requests carry the registered token in an
72	`Authorization: Bearer <token>` header. A missing header, a non-Bearer
73	scheme, a malformed bearer value, or an unregistered token yields
74	`401 Unauthorized` with `{"error": "unauthorized"}`.
75	
76	A valid credential that acts outside its bound organization or role yields
77	`403 Forbidden` with `{"error": "forbidden"}` and performs no write. The
78	`organizationId` in any request parameter or body field must equal the
79	token's registered organization; reading or writing another organization's
80	data is forbidden.
81	
82	- A `read` token may call only the state-free query and decision-computation
83	  entry points: the event list, aggregate, region, and replay (including
84	  replay comparison) queries, the reservation/alert listings,
85	  `GET /branches/{branchId}/resources`,
86	  `GET /snapshots/{snapshotId}/resources`,
87	  `GET /snapshots/{snapshotId}/reservations`,
88	  `GET /snapshots/{snapshotId}/events`,
89	  `GET /snapshots/{snapshotId}/events/region`,
90	  `GET /snapshots/{snapshotId}/events/aggregate`,
91	  `GET /snapshots/{snapshotId}/events/region/aggregate`,
92	  `POST /decisions/evaluate`, `POST /decisions/allocate`,
93	  `POST /branches/compare`, `POST /branches/compare/events`,
94	  `POST /branches/compare/reservations`,
95	  `POST /branches/compare/resources`, `POST /snapshots/compare`,
96	  `POST /snapshots/compare/events`,
97	  `POST /snapshots/compare/reservations`,
98	  `POST /snapshots/compare/resources`,
99	  `POST /snapshots/{snapshotId}/decisions/evaluate`, and the other
100	  read-only branch entry points.
101	- Committing an event or reservation, evaluating an alert, and creating a
102	  snapshot or branch are writes; only a `write` token may call them. A
103	  `read` token against a write entry point receives `403`. The authorization
104	  decision and the ledger/inventory mutation complete under one lock, so a
105	  rejected request never changes the ledger or inventory.
106	
107	Snapshots and branches belong to the organization that created them. A
108	snapshot captures only that organization's events, resource capacities, and
109	reservations, and the three summary counts count only that organization; a
110	branch forks only a snapshot owned by the same organization, and branch entry
111	points authenticate with the same rules as the main service. Snapshot and
112	branch names are unique across the whole service (not merely within one
113	organization), and accessing another organization's snapshot or branch by name
114	is `403`, never `404`.
115	
116	## Event ledger
117	
118	Events are held only in the server process: restarting (or starting a new
119	instance) begins with an empty ledger.
120	
121	### `POST /events`
122	
123	Requires `Content-Type: application/json`. The body must be a JSON object with
124	exactly these five top-level fields:
125	
126	| Field          | Rule                                      |
127	| -------------- | ----------------------------------------- |
128	| `eventId`      | non-empty string                          |
129	| `organizationId` | non-empty string                        |
130	| `type`         | non-empty string                          |
131	| `occurredAt`   | non-negative integer (no floats, no booleans) |
132	| `payload`      | JSON object                               |
133	
134	```bash
135	curl -X POST http://127.0.0.1:8000/events \
136	  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
137	  -d '{"eventId":"evt-1","organizationId":"org-1","type":"incident.created","occurredAt":100,"payload":{"severity":"low"}}'
138	```
139	
140	- `201 Created` — new event stored; the response is the same five-field JSON.
141	- `200 OK` — the same `eventId` was resubmitted with identical fields; the
142	  stored event is returned and nothing is added.
143	- `409 Conflict` (`{"error": "event_id_conflict"}`) — the `eventId` exists but
144	  the other fields differ.
145	- `415 Unsupported Media Type` — missing or unsupported `Content-Type`.
146	- `400 Bad Request` — body is not syntactically valid JSON.
147	- `422 Unprocessable Entity` — fields are missing, extra, or invalid
148	  (arrays at the top level, blank identifiers, floats, etc.).
149	
150	### `GET /events?organizationId=...`
151	
152	The `organizationId` query parameter must appear exactly once and be non-empty.
153	Returns `200` with `{"organizationId": "...", "events": [...]}`, where events
154	belong only to that organization and are sorted by `occurredAt`, then
155	`eventId`. An unknown organization returns `"events": []`. A missing, blank, or
156	duplicated parameter yields `422`.
157	
158	### `GET /events/aggregate?organizationId=...&type=...&windowSize=...`
159	
160	Counts stored events per time window, without modifying the ledger. Only
161	events matching both `organizationId` and `type` are counted; other
162	organizations' data is never included.
163	
164	Query parameters:
165	
166	| Parameter        | Rule                                                                 |
167	| ---------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------- |
168	| `organizationId` | required exactly once, non-empty string                              |
169	| `type`           | required exactly once, non-empty string                              |
170	| `windowSize`     | required exactly once, positive integer text (e.g. `60`)             |
171	| `from`           | optional; non-negative integer text, exactly once if present         |
172	| `to`             | optional; non-negative integer text, exactly once if present         |
173	
174	`from` and `to` must be omitted together or supplied together, and must
175	satisfy `from <= to`. A missing, duplicated, or invalid parameter yields
176	`422` with a JSON body containing a stable `error` field.
177	
178	Windows start at `0` and each covers `[start, end)` with
179	`end = start + windowSize`; an event belongs to a window when
180	`start <= occurredAt < end`. The `200` response is:
181	
182	```json
183	{
184	  "organizationId": "org-1",
185	  "type": "incident.created",
186	  "windowSize": 60,
187	  "from": null,
188	  "to": null,
189	  "windows": [{"start": 0, "end": 60, "count": 2}]
190	}
191	```
192	
193	- Without `from`/`to` (`from` and `to` echo back as `null`), only windows
194	  actually covered by matching events are returned; with no matching events
195	  `windows` is `[]`.
196	- With `from`/`to`, only events with `from <= occurredAt <= to` are counted,
197	  and every window intersecting the closed interval `[from, to]` is returned,
198	  including empty windows with `count: 0`.
199	- `windows` is sorted by `start` ascending; results are deterministic
200	  regardless of event insertion order, replays, or identical timestamps.
201	
202	```bash
203	curl 'http://127.0.0.1:8000/events/aggregate?organizationId=org-1&type=incident.created&windowSize=60&from=0&to=180'
204	```
205	
206	### Region attribution
207	
208	An event's region is the value of the `region` key in its `payload`. Only a
209	non-empty string attributes an event to a region: a missing key, an empty
210	string, or a non-string value means the event has no region. Region values
211	are matched verbatim (exact comparison, no trimming or normalization), and
212	regions need no registration — an unknown region simply matches zero events
213	and is never implicitly created. The region endpoints below are read-only:
214	they never write the event ledger, reservations, or alerts.
215	
216	### `GET /events/region?organizationId=...&region=...`
217	
218	Lists one organization's events attributed to one region. Both
219	`organizationId` and `region` must appear exactly once and be non-empty; a
220	missing, duplicated, or blank parameter yields `422`. Returns `200` with
221	`{"organizationId": "...", "region": "...", "events": [...]}`, where events
222	are sorted by `occurredAt`, then `eventId`, exactly like `GET /events`. An
223	unknown organization or region returns `"events": []`; other organizations'
224	events are never included. The body is compact JSON with keys sorted by code
225	point and a trailing newline.
226	
227	```bash
228	curl 'http://127.0.0.1:8000/events/region?organizationId=org-1&region=north'
229	```
230	
231	### `GET /events/region/aggregate?organizationId=...&region=...&type=...&windowSize=...`
232	
233	Counts per time window, using the exact same parameter rules, window
234	boundaries, ordering, and `from`/`to` semantics as
235	`GET /events/aggregate`, with an added `region` parameter that must appear
236	exactly once and be non-empty. Only events matching the organization,
237	region, and type are counted; events without a non-empty string payload
238	`region` never match. The `200` response mirrors the aggregate response with
239	one added `region` key (compact JSON, keys sorted by code point, trailing
240	newline):
241	
242	```json
243	{
244	  "organizationId": "org-1",
245	  "region": "north",
246	  "type": "incident.created",
247	  "windowSize": 60,
248	  "from": null,
249	  "to": null,
250	  "windows": [{"start": 0, "end": 60, "count": 2}]
251	}
252	```
253	
254	Without a range, only windows covered by matching events are returned; an
255	unknown region behaves like a zero-event match. With a range, every window
256	intersecting `[from, to]` is returned, including empty ones. Any parameter
257	problem — missing, duplicated, or blank values, a non-positive-integer
258	`windowSize`, unpaired or non-integer `from`/`to`, or `from > to` — yields
259	`422` with `{"error": "validation_error", ...}`.
260	
261	```bash
262	curl 'http://127.0.0.1:8000/events/region/aggregate?organizationId=org-1&region=north&type=incident.created&windowSize=60&from=0&to=180'
263	```
264	
265	### `POST /decisions/evaluate`
266	
267	A read-only, deterministic emergency decision over the same windows as the
268	aggregate endpoint. The ledger is never written to or changed by a decision
269	request. Requires `Content-Type: application/json`. The body must be a JSON
270	object containing exactly these fields:
271	
272	| Field            | Rule                                                          |
273	| ---------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------ |
274	| `organizationId` | required, non-empty string                                   |
275	| `type`           | required, non-empty string                                   |
276	| `windowSize`     | required, positive integer (no booleans, floats, or strings) |
277	| `threshold`      | required, positive integer (no booleans, floats, or strings) |
278	| `from`           | optional; non-negative integer, present only together with `to` |
279	| `to`             | optional; non-negative integer, present only together with `from` |
280	
281	Only events matching both `organizationId` and `type` are counted. Windows
282	start at `0` and cover `[start, start + windowSize)`. Without `from`/`to`,
283	only windows actually covered by matching events are considered; with a
284	range, events are filtered by the closed interval `from <= occurredAt <= to`
285	and every window intersecting that interval is considered, including empty
286	ones for audit reconciliation.
287	
288	The `200` response has a fixed shape:
289	
290	```json
291	{
292	  "organizationId": "org-1",
293	  "type": "incident.created",
294	  "windowSize": 60,
295	  "from": null,
296	  "to": null,
297	  "peakStart": 60,
298	  "peakCount": 2,
299	  "action": "observe"
300	}
301	```
302	
303	- `peakCount` is the largest window count and `peakStart` is that window's
304	  start; ties resolve to the earliest start, so results are reproducible
305	  regardless of event submission order.
306	- With no matching events (or no non-empty windows in range), `peakCount` is
307	  `0`, `peakStart` is `null`, and `action` is `"observe"`.
308	- `action` is `"escalate"` when `peakCount >= threshold`, otherwise
309	  `"observe"`.
310	- Unknown organizations or types compute as zero events and return normally;
311	  other organizations' data is never included.
312	
313	```bash
314	curl -X POST http://127.0.0.1:8000/decisions/evaluate \
315	  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
316	  -d '{"organizationId":"org-1","type":"incident.created","windowSize":60,"threshold":3}'
317	```
318	
319	- `415 Unsupported Media Type` — missing or unsupported `Content-Type`.
320	- `400 Bad Request` — body is not syntactically valid JSON; no decision is
321	  produced.
322	- `422 Unprocessable Entity` — a non-object body, missing or extra fields,
323	  invalid types, unpaired `from`/`to`, or out-of-range values.
324	
325	### `POST /decisions/allocate`
326	
327	A read-only, deterministic resource plan computed entirely from the request
328	body. Nothing is written to the event ledger, no earlier plan is inherited,
329	and concurrent requests cannot affect each other. Requires
330	`Content-Type: application/json`. The body must be a JSON object containing
331	exactly these fields:
332	
333	| Field            | Rule                                                          |
334	| ---------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------ |
335	| `organizationId` | required, non-empty string                                   |
336	| `demands`        | required array (may be empty) of demand objects              |
337	| `resources`      | required array (may be empty) of resource objects            |
338	
339	A demand object has exactly `demandId` (non-empty string, unique within the
340	request), `units` (positive integer), and `priority` (non-negative integer).
341	A resource object has exactly `resourceId` (non-empty string, unique within
342	the request) and `capacity` (positive integer). Booleans, floats, negative or
343	zero values where a positive integer is required, wrong element types, blank
344	or duplicate identifiers, and unknown fields are all rejected.
345	
346	Demands are handled by `priority` descending; ties resolve by `demandId` in
347	Unicode code-point order. A demand is placed wholly into the
348	lexicographically smallest `resourceId` whose remaining capacity covers its
349	units, and that capacity is deducted immediately. Demands are never split and
350	capacity is never oversold; a demand that fits in no remaining resource goes
351	to `unassigned` — priorities and units are never adjusted to place more
352	demands.
353	
354	The `200` response has a fixed shape:
355	
356	```json
357	{
358	  "organizationId": "org-1",
359	  "assignments": [
360	    {"demandId": "d-a", "resourceId": "r-a", "units": 2},
361	    {"demandId": "d-b", "resourceId": "r-b", "units": 4}
362	  ],
363	  "unassigned": ["d-big"],
364	  "totalUnits": 6
365	}
366	```
367	
368	- `assignments` lists `{"demandId", "resourceId", "units"}` objects in
369	  processing order.
370	- `unassigned` lists the demandIds that could not be placed, sorted by
371	  `demandId`.
372	- `totalUnits` counts only units that were assigned.
373	- Empty `demands`/`resources` arrays are valid and return empty results;
374	  identical submissions return byte-for-byte identical JSON.
375	
376	```bash
377	curl -X POST http://127.0.0.1:8000/decisions/allocate \
378	  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
379	  -d '{"organizationId":"org-1","demands":[{"demandId":"d-a","units":2,"priority":1}],"resources":[{"resourceId":"r-a","capacity":5}]}'
380	```
381	
382	- `415 Unsupported Media Type` — missing or unsupported `Content-Type`.
383	- `400 Bad Request` — body is not syntactically valid JSON.
384	- `422 Unprocessable Entity` — a non-object body, missing or extra fields,
385	  invalid types, duplicate or blank identifiers, or out-of-range values.
386	
387	## Reservation inventory
388	
389	Reservations are held only in the server process alongside the event ledger:
390	restarting (or starting a new instance) begins with empty inventory. The
391	first reservation that names a resource fixes that resource's capacity; it
392	is never rewritten afterwards.
393	
394	### `POST /reservations`
395	
396	Requires `Content-Type: application/json`. The body must be a JSON object
397	with exactly these five top-level fields:
398	
399	| Field           | Rule                                      |
400	| --------------- | ----------------------------------------- |
401	| `organizationId` | non-empty string                         |
402	| `reservationId` | non-empty string                          |
403	| `resourceId`    | non-empty string                          |
404	| `quantity`      | positive integer (no floats, no booleans) |
405	| `capacity`      | positive integer (no floats, no booleans) |
406	
407	```bash
408	curl -X POST http://127.0.0.1:8000/reservations \
409	  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
410	  -d '{"organizationId":"org-1","reservationId":"res-1","resourceId":"r-a","quantity":2,"capacity":5}'
411	```
412	
413	A successful response is compact JSON with stable key order, integer values,
414	and a trailing newline:
415	
416	```json
417	{"capacity":5,"occupied":2,"organizationId":"org-1","quantity":2,"remaining":3,"reservationId":"res-1","resourceId":"r-a"}
418	```
419	
420	`occupied` is the total confirmed quantity on the resource and `remaining`
421	is `capacity - occupied`; the balance can never go negative because the
422	check and the deduction commit atomically under one lock, so concurrent
423	requests cannot oversell a resource or lose each other's writes.
424	
425	- `201 Created` — new reservation committed; the first reservation for a
426	  resource also establishes its capacity.
427	- `200 OK` — the same `reservationId` was resubmitted with identical fields;
428	  nothing is counted twice and the balances are unchanged.
429	- `409 Conflict` (`{"error": "reservation_conflict"}`) — the `reservationId`
430	  exists but the other fields differ.
431	- `409 Conflict` (`{"error": "capacity_conflict"}`) — the resource already
432	  has a recorded capacity and the declared `capacity` differs; the recorded
433	  capacity is never rewritten.
434	- `409 Conflict` (`{"error": "capacity_exceeded"}`) — the quantity exceeds
435	  the resource's remaining balance; inventory and existing reservations are
436	  unchanged.
437	- `415 Unsupported Media Type` — missing or unsupported `Content-Type`.
438	- `400 Bad Request` — body is not syntactically valid JSON; no reservation
439	  is produced.
440	- `422 Unprocessable Entity` — a non-object body, missing or extra fields,
441	  blank or non-string identifiers, or non-positive/non-integer values.
442	
443	### `GET /reservations?organizationId=...`
444	
445	The `organizationId` query parameter must appear exactly once and be
446	non-empty. Returns `200` with `{"organizationId": "...", "reservations":
447	[...]}` containing only that organization's reservations, sorted by
448	`resourceId` then `reservationId` in Unicode code-point order. Each entry
449	carries `quantity`, the resource's `capacity`, and the resource-wide
450	`occupied` and `remaining` balances. An unknown organization returns
451	`"reservations": []`. A missing, blank, or duplicated parameter yields
452	`422`.
453	
454	## Alert suppression and escalation
455	
456	Alerts are held only in the main service process alongside the event
457	ledger; restarting (or starting a new instance) begins with no alerts.
458	Snapshots and branches never capture alerts, and the alert entry points
459	exist only on the main service — no `/branches/{branchId}/alerts/...`
460	paths are added.
461	
462	### `POST /alerts/evaluate`
463	
464	Requires `Content-Type: application/json`. The body must be a JSON object
465	containing exactly these fields:
466	
467	| Field               | Rule                                                          |
468	| ------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------ |
469	| `organizationId`    | required, non-empty string                                   |
470	| `type`              | required, non-empty string                                   |
471	| `windowSize`        | required, positive integer (no booleans, floats, or strings) |
472	| `threshold`         | required, positive integer (no booleans, floats, or strings) |
473	| `suppressionWindow` | required, positive integer (no booleans, floats, or strings) |
474	| `from`              | optional; non-negative integer, present only together with `to` |
475	| `to`                | optional; non-negative integer, present only together with `from` |
476	
477	The peak uses the exact same windowing as `POST /decisions/evaluate`: only
478	events matching both `organizationId` and `type` are counted, windows
479	start at `0` and cover `[start, start + windowSize)`, ties resolve to the
480	earliest window start, and an unknown organization or type computes as
481	zero events. The event ledger is never modified.
482	
483	- When the peak is below the threshold, `action` is `"observe"`, no alert
484	  is written, `alertId` is `null`, and `suppressedCount` is `null`.
485	- When the peak reaches the threshold, the peak start is compared with the
486	  most recent prior alert for the same organization and type:
487	  - `peakStart` not earlier than the prior start and at least
488	    `suppressionWindow` away (`peakStart - priorStart >=
489	    suppressionWindow`) creates a new alert; `action` is `"escalate"`,
490	    `alertId` is the new id (`alert-1`, `alert-2`, …, one global sequence
491	    across all organizations and types), and `suppressedCount` is `0`.
492	  - A peak start less than `suppressionWindow` after the prior alert's
493	    peak start increments that alert's suppression count instead; `action`
494	    is `"suppress"`, `alertId` is the prior alert's id, and
495	    `suppressedCount` is the new total. The first threshold hit for an
496	    organization/type always creates an alert.
497	
498	The suppression decision and the alert creation commit atomically under
499	one lock, so concurrent threshold hits cannot both open alerts or suppress
500	against a stale view. The `200` response echoes every request parameter
501	and adds the result fields (compact JSON, stable key order, integer values,
502	trailing newline):
503	
504	```json
505	{"action":"escalate","alertId":"alert-1","from":null,"organizationId":"org-1","peakCount":3,"peakStart":60,"suppressedCount":0,"suppressionWindow":120,"threshold":3,"to":null,"type":"incident.created","windowSize":60}
506	```
507	
508	```bash
509	curl -X POST http://127.0.0.1:8000/alerts/evaluate \
510	  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
511	  -d '{"organizationId":"org-1","type":"incident.created","windowSize":60,"threshold":3,"suppressionWindow":120}'
512	```
513	
514	- `415 Unsupported Media Type` — missing or unsupported `Content-Type`.
515	- `400 Bad Request` — body is not syntactically valid JSON; no alert is
516	  written.
517	- `422 Unprocessable Entity` — a non-object body, missing or extra fields,
518	  blank or non-string identifiers, booleans/floats where integers are
519	  required, non-positive values, unpaired `from`/`to`, or `from > to`.
520	
521	### `GET /alerts?organizationId=...`
522	
523	The `organizationId` query parameter must appear exactly once and be
524	non-empty. Returns `200` with `{"organizationId": "...", "alerts": [...]}`
525	containing only that organization's alerts. Each entry carries `alertId`,
526	`type`, `peakStart`, `threshold`, and `suppressedCount`, sorted by
527	`peakStart` ascending and then `alertId` in Unicode code-point order. An
528	unknown organization returns `"alerts": []`. A missing, blank, or
529	duplicated parameter yields `422`.
530	
531	## Snapshots and branches
532	
533	Snapshots capture the current main service state under a unique name so that
534	decisions can later be recomputed against that exact state. Branches fork a
535	snapshot into an isolated copy that supports the existing event, aggregate,
536	decision, and reservation entry points without sharing any mutable state with
537	the main service or with other branches.
538	
539	### Organization boundaries
540	
541	Every snapshot and branch is owned by the organization of the `write`
542	credential that created it, and all capture, naming, and visibility rules are
543	scoped to that boundary:
544	
545	- A snapshot captures **only the creator's own organization** — its events,
546	  the capacities of resources it reserves, and its reservations. Other
547	  organizations' events, reservation identifiers, and capacity records are
548	  neither captured nor summarized. The three counts in the response
549	  (`events`, `resources`, `reservations`) count only that organization. Two
550	  snapshots created from the same state return identical counts; another
551	  organization's data never changes them.

553	  data. Inside the branch, event and reservation names are compared only
554	  against that organization's own records. Another organization's event
555	  identifiers, reservation identifiers, and capacity records never cause a
556	  branch commit to conflict and never affect a branch balance.
557	- Snapshot and branch names are **unique across the whole service** and are
558	  owned by the creator's organization. A duplicate name conflicts regardless
559	  of which organization holds it: creating a snapshot with a name already in
560	  use returns `409` `snapshot_conflict` (the original snapshot is never
561	  rewritten), and creating a branch with a name already in use returns `409`
562	  `branch_conflict` (the existing branch is untouched). Names are not
563	  namespaced per organization.
564	- Using another organization's **snapshot name as a fork source**, or reading
565	  another organization's **branch by name**, returns `403 Forbidden`
566	  (`{"error": "forbidden"}`) with no content, even though the name exists. A
567	  name that has never appeared anywhere is the only case that yields `404`:
568	  a missing snapshot is `snapshot_not_found` and a missing branch is
569	  `branch_not_found`. Missing objects are never implicitly created.
570	- When creating a branch, snapshot ownership (`403`) is decided before the
571	  duplicate branch name (`409`); a foreign snapshot is forbidden even if the
572	  requested `branchId` is also taken. The snapshot list (`GET /snapshots`)
573	  and branch summaries are visible only within the owning organization.
574	- Authorization and the write happen under one lock for alert evaluation,
575	  snapshot creation, and branch creation alike. A rejected request leaves no
576	  alert, snapshot, or branch behind, and concurrent creations of the same
577	  name have exactly one winner; the loser receives the conflict response.
578	
579	Snapshots and branches capture only events, resource capacities, and
580	reservations — alerts are never captured, and the alert entry points remain
581	main-only with no branch-prefixed sub-paths. Like everything else here,
582	snapshots and branches live only in the server process and are cleared on
583	restart; there is no persistence, authorization, or replay across restarts.

585	### `POST /snapshots`

588	must be a JSON object containing exactly one field:

626	### `GET /snapshots/{snapshotId}/resources?organizationId=...`

628	A read-only listing of one snapshot's captured resource balances for the
629	caller's organization — the single-snapshot counterpart of
630	`POST /snapshots/compare/resources`, computed from the exact same balance
631	contract. Snapshots are immutable, so nothing in the snapshot, in any branch,
632	or in the main service is read for mutation or written: the main-service
633	event ledger, reservation inventory, and alert state are untouched, failed
634	requests leave no trace, and identical requests return byte-for-byte
635	identical JSON. Both `read` and `write` credentials may call it. The
636	`organizationId` query parameter must appear exactly once and be non-empty.
637	
638	The `200` response echoes the organization and snapshot identifiers and
639	carries one row per resource the organization reserves in the snapshot,
640	sorted by `resourceId` in Unicode code-point order. Each row reports the
641	three balances: `capacity` (fixed by the first captured reservation naming
642	the resource), `occupied` (the sum of every captured reservation the
643	organization holds against the resource — multiple reservations all count),

645	organizations never contribute (they are never captured), and a snapshot
646	with no resources returns an empty `resources` array. Because the balances
647	share the comparison's contract, comparing a snapshot with itself via

660	  -H 'Authorization: Bearer tok-1'

1037	captured at its creation time. Snapshots are immutable, so nothing in the
1038	snapshot, in any branch, or in the main service is read for mutation or
1039	written: the main-service event ledger, reservation inventory, and alert
1040	state are untouched, failed requests leave no trace, and identical requests
1041	return byte-for-byte identical JSON. Both `read` and `write` credentials
1042	may call it. Requires `Content-Type: application/json`. The body must be a
1043	JSON object containing exactly these fields:
1044	
1045	| Field            | Rule                                                          |
1046	| ---------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------ |
1047	| `organizationId` | required, non-empty string                                   |
1048	| `type`           | required, non-empty string                                   |
1049	| `windowSize`     | required, positive integer (no booleans, floats, or strings) |
1050	| `threshold`      | required, positive integer (no booleans, floats, or strings) |
1051	| `from`           | optional; non-negative integer, present only together with `to` |
1052	| `to`             | optional; non-negative integer, present only together with `from` |
1053	
1054	`from` and `to` must be omitted together or supplied together, and must
1055	satisfy `from <= to`. Only the snapshot's captured events matching both the
1056	caller's organization and `type` are counted; other organizations' data and
1057	events committed after capture never enter the result.
1058	
1059	Windows start at `0` and cover `[start, start + windowSize)` — boundaries
1060	identical to the main decision and the snapshot window comparison. Without
1061	`from`/`to`, only windows actually covered by matching captured events are
1062	considered; with a range, captured events are filtered by the closed
1063	interval `from <= occurredAt <= to` and every window intersecting that
1064	interval is considered, including empty ones counted as zero. The `200`
1065	response echoes the organization, snapshot, type, window width and the
1066	(possibly null) time range, and adds the peak result:
1067	
1068	```json
1069	{
1070	  "organizationId": "org-1",
1071	  "snapshotId": "snap-1",
1072	  "type": "incident.created",
1073	  "windowSize": 60,
1074	  "from": null,
1075	  "to": null,
1076	  "peakStart": 60,
1077	  "peakCount": 2,
1078	  "action": "observe"
1079	}
1080	```
1081	
1082	- `peakCount` is the largest window count and `peakStart` is that window's
1083	  start; ties resolve to the earliest start, so results are reproducible
1084	  regardless of event submission order.
1085	- With no matching events, `peakCount` is `0`, `peakStart` is `null`, and
1086	  `action` is `"observe"`.
1087	- `action` is `"escalate"` when `peakCount >= threshold`, otherwise
1088	  `"observe"`.
1089	- Because the peak shares the window comparison's contract, comparing a
1090	  snapshot with itself via `POST /snapshots/compare` reports this exact
1091	  `peakStart`, `peakCount`, and `action` on both the `left` and `right`
1092	  decision sides, item by item.
1093	
1094	The response is compact JSON with keys sorted by code point, integer values
1095	kept as integers, and one trailing newline:
1096	
1097	```json
1098	{"action":"observe","from":null,"organizationId":"org-1","peakCount":2,"peakStart":60,"snapshotId":"snap-1","to":null,"type":"incident.created","windowSize":60}
1099	```
1100	
1101	```bash
1102	curl -X POST http://127.0.0.1:8000/snapshots/snap-1/decisions/evaluate \
1103	  -H 'Authorization: Bearer tok-1' \
1104	  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
1105	  -d '{"organizationId":"org-1","type":"incident.created","windowSize":60,"threshold":3}'
1106	```
1107	
1108	The verdict order is fixed: the credential is checked first, then the
1109	request body, then the organization, and only then the snapshot name.
1110	
1111	- `401 Unauthorized` (`{"error": "unauthorized"}`) — the Bearer credential
1112	  is missing, malformed, or not registered; the body carries no business
1113	  content.
1114	- `415 Unsupported Media Type` — missing or unsupported `Content-Type`.
1115	- `400 Bad Request` — body is not syntactically valid JSON.
1116	- `422 Unprocessable Entity` (`validation_error`) — a non-object body, a
1117	  missing or extra field, a blank or non-string `organizationId`/`type`,
1118	  booleans/floats where integers are required, non-positive
1119	  `windowSize`/`threshold`, unpaired or non-integer `from`/`to`, or
1120	  `from > to`. No snapshot is created and nothing is written.
1121	- `403 Forbidden` (`{"error": "forbidden"}`) — the body's organization
1122	  differs from the credential's, or the named snapshot belongs to another
1123	  organization.
1124	- `404 Not Found` (`{"error": "snapshot_not_found"}`) — the snapshot name
1125	  has never existed; an evaluation never implicitly creates a snapshot.
1126	
1127	Every non-`200` result is read-only as well: a failed request creates no
1128	snapshot and changes no event, reservation, alert, or main-service state.
1129	
1130	### `POST /branches`
1131	
1132	Requires a `write` credential and `Content-Type: application/json`. The body
1133	must be a JSON object containing exactly these fields:
1134	
1135	| Field        | Rule                     |
1136	| ------------ | ------------------------ |
1137	| `branchId`   | non-empty string         |
1138	| `snapshotId` | non-empty string         |
1139	
1140	The new branch receives independent copies of the snapshot's events,
1141	resource capacities, and reservation balances (which hold only the snapshot
1142	owner organization's data).
1143	
1144	- `201 Created` — the branch summary is returned:
1145	
1146	```json
1147	{"branchId":"br-1","events":2,"reservations":1,"resources":1,"snapshotId":"snap-1"}
1148	```
1149	
1150	- `403 Forbidden` (`{"error": "forbidden"}`) — the named snapshot exists but
1151	  belongs to another organization (ownership is checked before the branch
1152	  name), or the credential is read-only. No branch is created and no snapshot
1153	  content is returned.
1154	- `404 Not Found` (`{"error": "snapshot_not_found"}`) — no snapshot with that
1155	  name has ever existed; no branch is created.
1156	- `409 Conflict` (`{"error": "branch_conflict"}`) — the snapshot is owned by
1157	  the caller but a branch with that `branchId` already exists anywhere in the
1158	  service. The existing branch is unaffected.
1159	- `415`, `400`, and `422` follow the same rules as other JSON write
1160	  endpoints; `422` (`validation_error`) covers missing, extra, blank, or
1161	  non-string fields.
1162	
1163	### `GET /branches/{branchId}`
1164	
1165	Returns `200` with the branch summary (see above) when the branch belongs to
1166	the caller's organization. A branch owned by another organization returns
1167	`403` with `{"error": "forbidden"}` and no content. Only a branch name that
1168	has never existed returns `404` with `{"error": "branch_not_found"}`.
1169	
1170	### Branch-prefixed entry points
1171	
1172	A known branch exposes the existing endpoints under
1173	`/branches/{branchId}/...`, with identical request contracts, query
1174	validation, ordering, and window semantics:
1175	
1176	| Method | Path                                      | Effect                                    |
1177	| ------ | ----------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------- |
1178	| GET    | `/branches/{branchId}/events`             | list the branch's events                  |
1179	| GET    | `/branches/{branchId}/events/aggregate`   | aggregate the branch's events             |
1180	| POST   | `/branches/{branchId}/events`             | commit an event into the branch only      |
1181	| POST   | `/branches/{branchId}/decisions/evaluate` | evaluate against the branch's events only |
1182	| GET    | `/branches/{branchId}/reservations`       | list the branch's reservations            |
1183	| GET    | `/branches/{branchId}/resources`          | list the branch's resource balances       |
1184	| POST   | `/branches/{branchId}/reservations`       | reserve against branch balances only      |
1185	
1186	- Branch event commits honor `415`, `400`, `422`, identical-replay (`200`),
1187	  and `event_id_conflict` (`409`); writes stay in the branch. Name and
1188	  capacity comparisons run only against the owning organization's records
1189	  that were forked into the branch, so another organization's event
1190	  identifiers, reservation identifiers, and capacity records never trigger a
1191	  conflict and never affect a branch balance.
1192	- Branch reservation commits honor `415`, `400`, `422`, and the replay and
1193	  capacity rules: identical replays return `200` without double counting,
1194	  while `reservation_conflict`, `capacity_conflict`, and
1195	  `capacity_exceeded` still return `409`; a failed commit never changes the
1196	  branch inventory.
1197	- Branch list and aggregate queries apply the same parameter rules as the
1198	  main endpoints; missing, duplicated, or empty parameters return `422` with
1199	  `validation_error`.
1200	- Branch evaluation is read-only over branch events, and branch aggregates
1201	  never count main-service events; repeated identical requests return
1202	  identical results.
1203	- No branch operation creates or rolls back main-service state, and branches
1204	  never observe each other's writes. Unknown sub-paths under a known branch
1205	  return the standard JSON `404`; sub-paths under an unknown branch return
1206	  `branch_not_found`.
1207	- The region queries (`/events/region` and `/events/region/aggregate`) are
1208	  main-only; no branch-prefixed region paths are added.
1209	- `/decisions/allocate` remains a main-only, stateless endpoint.
1210	
1211	### `GET /branches/{branchId}/resources?organizationId=...`
1212	
1213	A read-only listing of one branch's current resource balances for the
1214	caller's organization — the single-branch counterpart of
1215	`POST /branches/compare/resources`, computed from the exact same balance
1216	contract. Nothing in the branch, in any other branch, or in the main
1217	service is read for mutation or written, alert state is untouched, and
1218	identical requests return byte-for-byte identical JSON. Both `read` and
1219	`write` credentials may call it. The `organizationId` query parameter
1220	must appear exactly once and be non-empty.
1221	
1222	The `200` response echoes the organization and branch identifiers and
1223	carries one row per resource the organization reserves in the branch,
1224	sorted by `resourceId` in Unicode code-point order. Each row reports the
1225	three balances: `capacity` (fixed by the first reservation naming the
1226	resource in the branch), `occupied` (the sum of every reservation the
1227	organization holds against the resource in that branch — multiple
1228	reservations all count), and `remaining` (`capacity - occupied`).
1229	Reservations of other organizations never contribute, and a branch with
1230	no resources returns an empty `resources` array. Because the balances
1231	share the comparison's contract, comparing a branch with itself via
1232	`POST /branches/compare/resources` reports every listed row as `equal`.
1233	
1234	The response is compact JSON with keys sorted by code point, integer
1235	values kept as integers, and one trailing newline:
1236	
1237	```json
1238	{"branchId":"br-1","organizationId":"org-1","resources":[{"capacity":10,"occupied":3,"remaining":7,"resourceId":"res-a"},{"capacity":4,"occupied":1,"remaining":3,"resourceId":"res-b"}]}
1239	```
1240	
1241	```bash
1242	curl 'http://127.0.0.1:8000/branches/br-1/resources?organizationId=org-1' \
1243	  -H 'Authorization: Bearer tok-1'
1244	```
1245	
1246	The verdict order is fixed: the credential is checked first, then the
1247	query shape, then the organization, and only then the branch name.
1248	
1249	- `401 Unauthorized` (`{"error": "unauthorized"}`) — the Bearer credential
1250	  is missing, malformed, or not registered.
1251	- `422 Unprocessable Entity` (`validation_error`) — the `organizationId`
1252	  parameter is missing, duplicated, or blank.
1253	- `403 Forbidden` (`{"error": "forbidden"}`) — the parameter's
1254	  organization differs from the credential's, or the named branch belongs
1255	  to another organization.
1256	- `404 Not Found` (`{"error": "branch_not_found"}`) — the branch name has
1257	  never existed; a listing never implicitly creates a branch.
1258	
1259	Every non-`200` result is read-only as well: a failed request creates no
1260	branch and changes no event, reservation, alert, or main-service state.
1261	
1262	### `POST /branches/compare`
1263	
1264	A read-only comparison of two existing branches' window counts and peak
1265	decisions. Each side recomputes its window counts and peak from that
1266	branch's own events only; nothing in either branch, in any other branch, or
1267	in the main service is read for mutation or written, and identical
1268	submissions return byte-for-byte identical JSON. Both `read` and `write`
1269	credentials may call it. Requires `Content-Type: application/json` and a
1270	Bearer credential bound to the request's `organizationId`. The body must be
1271	a JSON object containing exactly these fields:
1272	
1273	| Field            | Rule                                                          |
1274	| ---------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------ |
1275	| `organizationId` | required, non-empty string; both branches must belong to it |
1276	| `left`           | required, non-empty branch name (the left-hand side)         |
1277	| `right`          | required, non-empty branch name (the right-hand side)        |
1278	| `type`           | required, non-empty string                                   |
1279	| `windowSize`     | required, positive integer (no booleans, floats, or strings) |
1280	| `threshold`      | required, positive integer (no booleans, floats, or strings) |
1281	| `from`           | optional; non-negative integer, present only together with `to` |
1282	| `to`             | optional; non-negative integer, present only together with `from` |
1283	
1284	Using the same branch name for `left` and `right` is legal; the two sides
1285	are then equal by construction. Window division matches the aggregate and
1286	decision entry points exactly: windows start at `0` and cover
1287	`[start, start + windowSize)`, and an event counts toward the window of
1288	`floor(occurredAt / windowSize) * windowSize`.
1289	
1290	- Without `from`/`to`, the `windows` rows cover the **union** of the windows
1291	  hit by matching events on either side, aligned row-by-row by `start`
1292	  ascending. A window hit by only one side shows the other side's count as
1293	  `0`. When neither side has a matching event, `windows` is `[]`.
1294	- With `from`/`to`, only events in the closed interval
1295	  `from <= occurredAt <= to` count, and **every** window intersecting that
1296	  interval gets a row, including windows empty on both sides.
1297	- Each row is `{"start", "leftCount", "rightCount", "equal"}`, with
1298	  `equal` true exactly when the two counts agree.
1299	- `decision.left` and `decision.right` each carry `peakStart`,
1300	  `peakCount`, and `action`: the peak is the largest window count, ties
1301	  resolve to the earliest window start, and `action` is `"escalate"` when
1302	  the peak reaches `threshold` and `"observe"` otherwise. `decision.equal`
1303	  is true exactly when the two sides' peak results agree. An empty side has
1304	  `peakStart: null`, `peakCount: 0`, and `action: "observe"`.
1305	
1306	The `200` response is compact JSON with keys sorted by code point, integer
1307	values kept as integers, booleans kept as booleans, and one trailing
1308	newline:
1309	
1310	```json
1311	{"decision":{"equal":false,"left":{"action":"observe","peakCount":2,"peakStart":0},"right":{"action":"escalate","peakCount":3,"peakStart":60}},"from":null,"left":"br-a","organizationId":"org-1","right":"br-b","threshold":3,"to":null,"type":"incident.created","windowSize":60,"windows":[{"equal":false,"leftCount":2,"rightCount":1,"start":0},{"equal":false,"leftCount":0,"rightCount":3,"start":60}]}
1312	```
1313	
1314	```bash
1315	curl -X POST http://127.0.0.1:8000/branches/compare \
1316	  -H 'Authorization: Bearer tok-1' \
1317	  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
1318	  -d '{"organizationId":"org-1","left":"br-a","right":"br-b","type":"incident.created","windowSize":60,"threshold":3}'
1319	```
1320	
1321	- `401 Unauthorized` — the Bearer credential is missing, malformed, or not
1322	  registered.
1323	- `403 Forbidden` (`{"error": "forbidden"}`) — the credential is bound to a
1324	  different organization, or one of the named branches belongs to another
1325	  organization. The organization decision happens before branch names are
1326	  inspected, and branches are checked in the fixed order `left` then
1327	  `right` (a missing left outranks any problem on the right).
1328	- `404 Not Found` (`{"error": "branch_not_found"}`) — either `left` or
1329	  `right` has never existed as a branch. Both participating branches must
1330	  already exist; a comparison never implicitly creates a branch.
1331	- `415 Unsupported Media Type` — missing or unsupported `Content-Type`.
1332	- `400 Bad Request` — body is not syntactically valid JSON.
1333	- `422 Unprocessable Entity` (`validation_error`) — a non-object body, a
1334	  missing or extra field, a blank or non-string `organizationId`/`left`/
1335	  `right`/`type`, non-positive-integer `windowSize`/`threshold`, unpaired or
1336	  non-integer `from`/`to`, or `from > to`.
1337	
1338	Every non-`200` result is read-only as well: a failed comparison creates no
1339	branch and changes no event, reservation, or decision state.
1340	
1341	### `POST /branches/compare/events`
1342	
1343	A read-only, event-level comparison of two existing branches. Where
1344	`POST /branches/compare` aligns window counts, this entry point aligns the
1345	two branches' events by `eventId` and reports the deterministic difference
1346	summary. Nothing in either branch, in any other branch, or in the main
1347	service is read for mutation or written, and identical submissions return
1348	byte-for-byte identical JSON. Both `read` and `write` credentials may call
1349	it. Requires `Content-Type: application/json` and a Bearer credential bound
1350	to the request's `organizationId`. The body must be a JSON object
1351	containing exactly these fields:
1352	
1353	| Field            | Rule                                                          |
1354	| ---------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------ |
1355	| `organizationId` | required, non-empty string; both branches must belong to it |
1356	| `left`           | required, non-empty branch name (the left-hand side)         |
